summary: P3E14 process-local retrieval measurements and bounded opt-in query diagnostics, separate from project authority and durable history.

configuration.bounds: Required v7 object with exactly these fields. Retained requests 0..256, query bytes 1..8192, at most 32 unique valid project IDs. Empty capture list is metadata-only; wildcards and capture with zero retention are rejected. Earlier service-config versions are rejected; no legacy reader.

currentExtension: P3E17 knowledge policy is independent of unchanged observability fields. versions below identifies the original P3E14 verification, not current Server deployment. Session bootstrap measures one ordinary Brief service attempt per member; these counters are not outer HTTP request counts.

api.metrics: GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval, no query parameters, administrator only. Schema shin.retrieval-metrics.v1, instance_id, scope process-lifetime-authorized-service-attempts, fixed operation/selector cells, counters and explicit duration histogram buckets. No query text, project labels, request IDs or paths in metric dimensions.
api.requests: GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval/requests?after=0&limit=20[&instance_id=...], administrator only. Schema shin.retrieval-request-page.v1. Limit1..32; after is a nonnegative integer. Nonzero after requires this process instance_id; another instance is 409/telemetry-instance-mismatch. Report oldest_available_sequence, latest_sequence, gap and next_after. Empty or evicted history is never complete request history.
api.resultBoundary: Existing search/Brief/Pack response bodies are unchanged. These records describe Server requests, not a claim about which LLM generated them. No HTTP response correlation header or automatic agent action is added.

requestRecords.identity: Each completed attempt has a process-local monotonic sequence, operation, selector kind, authorized project/selector IDs and wall timestamp. Successful selection identity comes from the actual returned result; unavailable failure provenance stays null.
requestRecords.capture: Only explicitly allowlisted projects with a validated request may retain the request JSON. Bound the encoded input by max_query_bytes; omit oversized input entirely, never truncate it into a misleading replay. Distinguish disabled, invalid-request, captured, omitted-budget and capture-failed. The collector does not read transport headers or authentication credentials, exception messages or response source fragments. Sensitive text embedded in an opted-in query is not automatically removed.
requestRecords.privacy: Query or task text can itself contain sensitive data. Opt-in is not a secret scrubber or anonymization guarantee. Administrators must review project policy before enabling capture, protect exported diagnostics, and never submit credentials in queries. The default capture list is empty; no consumer is enrolled here.
requestRecords.retention: Keep at most configured records and 2MiB encoded record payload; evict oldest diagnostic records and count evictions. This is not a total RSS bound. Restart loses all process-local data. No TTL, disk persistence, PostgreSQL query journal or durable export guarantee in this slice.
requestRecords.isolation: Recording failure must not change a retrieval result. No source/index/consumer writes, telemetry SQL transactions, new background worker or dependency on an external collector. Diagnostic reads do not increment retrieval measurements.

acceptance: Fixed counter/histogram cells and phase totals under concurrent calls
Bounded count/byte retention and explicit eviction/restart cursor gaps
Default absence of query text and allowlisted validated capture only
Correct null quality on failures and incomplete Pack distinct from failure
Telemetry cannot alter evidence or authorize access
Measured recording overhead and full companion regression gates
later: P3E15 builds an explicit administrative capture and typed PostgreSQL reports from this bounded buffer; see shin-retrieval-journal-v1. Continuous delivery, retention and optional OpenTelemetry export remain separate. Keep client-reported follow-up actions/evaluations distinct from Server measurements. Publication-history lifecycle remains planned; this P3E14 slice does not solve it.
